messages.subject: Test information curves?
parts:
Email: 

Hi Phil. I was wondering if I could bother you for another couple of questions.

How to plot the test characteristic curve?

Test information usually has 1 as a lower bound, which makes the standard error of measurement have a maximum of 1 (if we know nothing about the individual our standard error of measurement is the standard deviation of theta. Can you let me know your thoughts?

Thanks again,

Reply: 

Hi,

I don't think that that is correct. The information function can and should approach 0 at ±∞ since it is based on the amount of slope in the item response curves. At the point inflection in the curves is where the maximum information is found, but near the tails there will be little to no information as the θ's become extreme, and eventually have no slope at all (hence no information). I believe what you are thinking of is EAP estimates of θ (MAP as well), in which case yes you would be correct. To plot the test curves in mirt just use plot(object), and you can change the type this way to by stating plot(object, type = 'info'). Cheers.

Phil
